stances.claim: Duterte's career-jurist-only promotion policy, whether intended or not, helps CJ Peralta achieve his first goal of backlog elimination, because justices who already disposed of the CA backlog under Reyes can repeat the feat at the SC.

stances.claim: First-level courts (133 cases per sala average) show no palpable congestion and do not need urgent action; the congestion crisis is concentrated in the second-level RTCs (582 cases per sala average, exacerbated by 25% sala vacancies).
stances.rhetorical_move: quantitative differentiation (rejecting blanket diagnosis with arithmetic)

stances.claim: The JBC's decision to open only 30 of the 100 RTC Judges-at-Large posts created by RA 11459 is a significant under-utilization that will limit the dent made in the 640,000-case backlog; all 100 should have been opened.
stances.confidence: asserted with deference marker ('with due respect to the Supreme Court and the JBC')

stances.claim: Even with all 100 new posts, the average load drops only to 533 -- still a large number -- meaning the law alone is insufficient; what is needed is a combination of full filling of RA 11459 posts plus tactical deployment to the most-congested salas.

stances.claim: Solving even 50% of the horrendous SC + RTC congestion within Peralta's 2.5-year term would earn him acclaim; this is the realistic benchmark for legacy.
stances.rhetorical_move: lowered-bar benchmark setting (acclaim attached to partial success)

notable_anecdotes: The arithmetic spectacle: 582 cases per RTC sala ÷ 25 working days = 23 hearings calendared per day, which 'will take almost one whole day' just to read aloud -- leaving no time for actual trial. CJ uses pure arithmetic to demonstrate institutional impossibility.
The extreme distribution disparity -- some RTCs with 5,000 cases, some with just 50 -- used as a quiet rebuke to the JBC for not concentrating Judges-at-Large where they would matter most.
Andres B. Reyes Jr.'s 7-year disposal of the CA backlog cited as living proof that 'sheer hard work and automated monitoring' can do the same in the SC; the same justices are now in the SC.
The 'My limited space bars me from digging deeper' closing -- a recurring CJ device for promising follow-up analysis on a sub-topic he won't fit in 750 words.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban turns to the second prong of CJ Peralta's backlog elimination goal: the trial courts. He observes that President Duterte's policy of promoting only CA and Sandiganbayan magistrates to the SC -- though it breaks the tradition of balancing insiders with justice secretaries, solicitors-general and academics -- may unintentionally help Peralta, because the same justices who disposed of the CA backlog under then-Presiding Justice Andres B. Reyes Jr. can repeat the feat in the SC. Turning to trial-court congestion, he uses arithmetic to differentiate the two levels: first-level courts hold ~133 cases per sala (no palpable congestion), while RTCs hold ~582 per sala -- meaning 23 hearings would need to be calendared per working day, leaving no time for actual trial. The crisis is worsened by ~25% sala vacancies and grossly uneven distribution (5,000 cases in some salas, 50 in others). Congress's response, RA 11459 -- creating 100 RTC and 50 Municipal Judges-at-Large positions deployable to congested salas -- is sound, but the JBC has opened only 30 + 20 of those positions, less than half. Panganiban argues, 'with due respect to the Supreme Court and the JBC,' that all 100 RTC posts should be opened; even then the average drops only to 533, still large, but better than the smaller dent now planned. He closes endorsing Peralta's valiant effort: solving even 50% of this horrendous congestion within his 2.5-year term would earn him true acclaim.
